messages.subject: Re: SNP order causing an error
messages.body_plain:
Hi, everyone.

I am facing the same problem as discussed here.
Using the commonfactorGWAS function, we perform it separately for each chromosome.
It is strange that the error message was shown only for chromosome 4:

error calling combine function:
<simpleError in match.names(clabs, names(xi)): names do not match previous names>

Error in `colnames<-`(`*tmp*`, value = colnamesresults) :
  attempt to set 'colnames' on an object with less than two dimensions
Calls: commonfactorGWAS -> colnames<-
Execution halted

For the other chromosomes except for chr4, the codes successfully completed and I got the results.
If you already find a solution to this problem, please let me know.

Best Regards,
Ryo

messages.subject: Re: Obtaining p-values for LDSC
messages.body_plain:
the most straightforward way is to specify a model in genomic sem that represents a saturated covariance matrix and then look at the standardized output and associated SEs.
Michel's Rpub actually shows this as an example: https://rpubs.com/MichelNivard/640145
as with below "the ratio of the estimate to its standard error can be used to determine the p value using the pnorm function in R, taking care about whether you are interested in a 1 or 2 tailed p value..."
elliot

messages.subject_clean: Question about cfgwas memory usage for many traits
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

Do you know how possible it is to run the commonfactor GWAS on about 42 GWAS summary statistic files? In a sample of 3/42 traits, it took about 90 GB of memory and had a run time of 11 hours with 8 cores. Do you know if that is within the realm of memory that it is expected to take given I have ~1,100,000 SNPs?

I have submitted a linux job to a sun grid engine about two weeks ago, and I am additionally working to trouble shoot it with the maintainers of the cluster. Though, it it seeming like it is taking a very large amount of memory that I am not currently sure if it is possible to run this function on 40-50 traits as I originally intended to.

Thank you,
Rama

messages.subject: Re: Question about cfgwas memory usage for many traits
messages.subject_clean: Question about cfgwas memory usage for many traits
messages.body_plain:
Hi Rama,

This is on the higher end of my expectations, but definitely still seems sensible to me. If you are running on Linux (especially on the sun grid) make sure to follow our advice detailed in https://github.com/GenomicSEM/GenomicSEM/wiki/1.1-For-Linux-users
If this is not set up properly it could lead to large amounts of memory being wasted, so keep an eye on the running R processes and see if there aren't too many (with 8 cores you would expect 9 processes, 1 main thread and 8 additional ones, one for each core). If you followed our advice and are still seeing too many threads, send this information on to the sun grid engineers, they might have another kind of multi-threading background set up that interferes with this.

If that doesn't help (or was already fixed) you could try either chunking your data and spreading the load across different nodes, or reducing the number of threads (though especially the latter will of course impact compute time).

Those are the only software-based solutions I see to your issue. That being said the best solutions would of course be to inquire about availability of high-memory nodes in your cluster. I expect this to scale somewhat linearly, so 128GB  (256 if you want to be on the safe side) might well suffice for your 40-50 traits. If those are not available you could look into memory-optimized cloud solutions such as Google M1/M2 instances https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/memory-optimized-machines or AWS EC2 R5/R6 instances https://aws.amazon.com/ec2/instance-types/

Best,
Matthijs

messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I am using two different hg builds (hg38 and hg19) for 6 traits for commonfactorGWAS. Though I could successfully obtain 1-factor GWAS sumstats, but to derive polygenic risk scores based on this 1-factor GWAS summary statistics, LDpred2 gives an error as I have used two different hg builds to construct sumstats. Is there a way where I can harmonize after the common factor GWAS step to circumvent the error in LDpred2?

Thanks in advance for any inputs.

Best Regards,
Rajini

> So model fits the data well (briefly: the chisq test, which tests the model against a freely estimated covariance matrix isnt significant, which means the model doest describe the covariance significantly worse, CFI is 1, CFI ranges form 0 to 1 and is a comparison against an "empty" model where the traits are uncorrelated, 1 means good ft compared to an empty model. then the SRMR quantifies the (weighted I believe) squared difference between the observed and expected covariance matrix, its lowish here, which is good.
>
> This all being said, the model fits the covariance matrix well, but the factor doest explain a lot of the heritable variation in for example TS ( .114^2 / (.114^2 + .199) = ~6%)
>
> so if you added TS because you are interested in genetic effects on TS be forewarned this factor isn't really a reflection of TS (because TS doest correlate to highly with the other traits I think)

> Your model is slower than usual I'd sya, but not entirely unheard off. To speed things up you can specify starting values near (but not at!) the final estimates and perhaps things go a bit quicker.
